items.name: Python 3.14
items.desc: The python.org build, with pip and the py launcher it carries.

items.name: Java (Temurin JDK 21)
items.desc: Eclipse Temurin, the mainstream free OpenJDK build. LTS release.

items.name: C++ build tools (MSVC)
items.desc: Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools with the C++ workload - the Microsoft compiler, linker and Windows SDK, without the Visual Studio IDE.
items.riskNote: The largest thing here by a wide margin: 3-7 GB depending on what the recommended components pull in, and it can take well over half an hour on a slow connection. The run waits for it.

items.name: Git
items.desc: Git for Windows, with Git Bash and the credential manager.

items.name: Eclipse IDE for Java
items.desc: The Eclipse Java IDE, with the Java runtime it ships with. winget installs it as a portable app, so it has no Start menu entry: run eclipse from a terminal, or pin eclipse.exe from winget's Packages folder.

items.settingsPath: Re-create the shortcut yourself, or reinstall the program.
items.name: Install without desktop shortcuts
items.desc: Clears the desktop shortcuts the apps above create as they install. Only shortcuts that appeared during this run are touched; anything already on your desktop stays.
items.riskNote: Removes any .lnk or .url that appears on your desktop or the shared desktop while the run is going. In practice that is the installers, but a shortcut you happen to create yourself mid-run would go too. They go to the Recycle Bin.

items.name: 7-Zip
items.desc: Archive tool that opens everything Explorer will not.

items.name: MakeMKV
items.desc: Reads Blu-ray and DVD discs into MKV files.
items.riskNote: Free while in beta, and the beta key it ships with expires periodically - the vendor publishes a new one. Ripping discs you do not own, or breaking copy protection, may be unlawful where you live.

items.name: Adobe Photoshop (via Creative Cloud)
items.desc: Installs the Adobe Creative Cloud desktop app, which is how Photoshop is installed and licensed.
items.riskNote: Photoshop itself is not distributed as a standalone package this can fetch - Adobe ships it through Creative Cloud only. This puts Creative Cloud on the machine; Photoshop is then installed from inside it, and needs a paid Adobe subscription. Creative Cloud also adds background services and a startup entry of its own. Right after Adobe ships a new installer the winget package can be a step behind and refuse it, until winget catches up.

items.name: Microsoft PowerToys
items.desc: Microsoft's utility suite: the Alt+Space launcher, window snapping layouts, a color picker, and a few dozen more.

items.name: PowerToys Run on Alt+Space
items.desc: The launcher: start typing to find an app, a file, a calculation, or a setting. Current PowerToys ships it switched off in favour of Command Palette on Win+Alt+Space, so this turns it on, for the account that runs the toolkit.
items.riskNote: Configures PowerToys, so it only does something if PowerToys is installed - tick Microsoft PowerToys above if it is not. The setting is written either way and is read the first time PowerToys starts. The Copilot app claims Alt+Space as well; removing it under AI frees the shortcut.
